cor-mc-scheffe-f.title: The F test and Scheffé’s intervals
cor-mc-scheffe-f.title_html: The F test and Scheffé’s intervals
cor-mc-scheffe-f.html:
In the setting of @thm-mc-scheffe(b), for every d∈Rq:

  1. 𝛉maxa≠0(a⊤θ^−a⊤d)2s2a⊤Wa=qF, attained at 𝛉a=W−1(θ^−d);

  2. the level-α F test rejects 𝛃Λ⊤β=d iff at least one statement 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β=a⊤d, 𝛌λ=Λa, is Scheffé-rejected;

  3. if 𝛃Λ⊤β=d is true, the probability that any of these statements is Scheffé-rejected is exactly α. For any 𝛃β, the probability of Scheffé-rejecting at least one true statement 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β=c, 𝛌λ∈C(Λ), is at most α.

def-mc-error-rates.title: Error rates of a family
def-mc-error-rates.html:
For a multiple testing procedure and a given value of the parameters:

  1. the familywise error rate is FWER=Pr(V≥1), the probability of at least one false rejection;

  2. the per-family error rate is PFER=E(V), the expected number of false rejections, and the per-comparison error rate is PCER=E(V)/m;

  3. the false discovery proportion is Q=V/max(R,1), which is V/R when something is rejected and 0 otherwise, and the false discovery rate is its expectation, FDR=E(Q).

A procedure controls one of these rates at level α if the rate is at most α for every value of the parameters.

def-mc-strong-control.title: Strong and weak control
def-mc-strong-control.html: A procedure controls the familywise error rate strongly at level α if Pr(V≥1)≤α for every value of the parameters, and weakly if Pr(V≥1)≤α whenever all of H1,…,Hm are true.

def-mc-studentized-range.title: Studentized range
def-mc-studentized-range.html: Let Z1,…,Zg be independent N(0,1) variables, g≥2, and let V∼χ2(ν) be independent of them. The law of Q=maxkZk−minkZkV/ν is the studentized range distribution with parameters g and ν. Its upper α point is written qα(g,ν).

eq-mc-bonferroni-interval.html: 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃λj⊤β^±tν,α/(2k)se(λj⊤β^),j=1,…,k,

eq-mc-function-vector.html: 𝛌𝛃𝛒𝛃𝛍𝛌𝛃𝛒𝛌𝛌𝛒𝛒𝛒𝛒λ⊤β=ρ⊤Xβ=v⊤μ,λ⊤β^=ρ⊤MY=v⊤Y,λ⊤Gλ=ρ⊤XGX⊤ρ=ρ⊤Mρ=‖v‖2.

eq-mc-independent-rate.html: FWER=1−Pr(no rejection)=1−(1−α)m.

exm-mc-bh-screening.title: One hundred candidate regressors
exm-mc-bh-screening.html:
A simulated regression has n=250 observations, an intercept and 100 regressors with independent standard normal entries, leaving ν=149 error degrees of freedom. The first 10 slopes are nonzero, each chosen so that the noncentrality of its t statistic is 3; the other 90 are zero. The 100 two-sided t tests are run on one data set at level 0.05:

procedure rejections of which false
unadjusted, p≤0.05 9 2
Bonferroni 1 0
Holm 1 0
BH, q=0.05 7 1

Bonferroni’s threshold is 0.05/100=0.0005, and only one p-value is below it. The BH line reaches 7×0.05/100=0.0035 at rank 7, and the seventh smallest p-value is 0.0034 (Figure 13.5.1). Six of the seven BH discoveries are real.

exm-mc-chance.title: All pairs of equal means
exm-mc-chance.html: Take g groups of 5 observations each, with all group means equal, and compare every pair with an unadjusted two-sided t test at level 0.05, using the pooled variance estimate on g(5−1) degrees of freedom. The listing simulates 20000 data sets for each g. For g=3,5,7,10 (so 3,10,21,45 pairs), the proportion of data sets with at least one significant pair is 0.116,0.265,0.412,0.589. Independent tests would give 0.143, 0.401, 0.659 and 0.901. The average number of significant pairs is 0.15, 0.50, 1.08 and 2.23, in each case 0.05 times the number of pairs up to simulation error. Figure 13.1.1 plots the familywise rate against the number of tests.

exm-mc-holm-education.title: Holm for the education pairs
exm-mc-holm-education.html: For the 21 pairwise comparisons of @exm-mc-tukey-education the smallest p-value is 1.1×10−5. Bonferroni’s threshold is 0.05/21=0.00238, and 8 of the p-values fall below it. Holm’s procedure starts at the same threshold but relaxes it after each rejection. It rejects 10 hypotheses: the tenth smallest p-value is 0.0037, below its threshold 0.05/12, and the eleventh, 0.0126, exceeds 0.05/11=0.0045, so the procedure stops.

exm-mc-holm-power.title: Ten regression coefficients
exm-mc-holm-power.html: A regression has an intercept and ten centred, mutually orthogonal regressors, with n=40. The ten t statistics for the slopes are then Tj=Zj/V/29 with independent Zj∼N(δj,1) and a shared V∼χ2(29) (@thm-opt-sampling). Let k of the slopes be nonzero, each with δj=3.5, and test all ten at familywise level 0.05. Figure 13.4.1 shows the result of 20000 simulated data sets for each k. All three procedures keep the familywise error rate at or below 0.05, up to simulation error. The average power of Bonferroni’s procedure, the proportion of nonzero slopes it detects, hardly depends on k: it is 0.675 with one nonzero slope and 0.676 with five or nine. Šidák’s is larger by a few thousandths. Holm’s power is 0.675 with one nonzero slope, 0.718 with five and 0.794 with nine.

exm-mc-newman-keuls.title: Newman–Keuls without strong control
exm-mc-newman-keuls.html: Take g=10 groups of 5 observations, with the true means equal in pairs and the five pairs far apart, and ν=40. The larger ranges are always significant, so the procedure reaches every pair and tests it with qα(2,ν), the critical value of a single unadjusted comparison. In 10000 simulated data sets, the Newman–Keuls procedure declares some pair of equal means different in a proportion 0.219 of them. Five independent level-0.05 tests would err with probability 0.226; the shared s lowers the rate slightly, as @prp-mc-sidak implies. Tukey’s intervals err in 0.011 of the data sets.

exm-mc-protected-lsd.title: The protected LSD without strong control
exm-mc-protected-lsd.title_html: The protected LSD without strong control
exm-mc-protected-lsd.html: With g=10 groups of 5 observations and all means equal, the simulation below gives a familywise error rate of 0.049, as @prp-mc-gatekeeper promises. Now move one mean far from the other nine, which remain equal. The F test rejects in essentially every data set, the gate is always open, and the 36 pairwise comparisons among the nine equal means are made without adjustment. The familywise error rate rises to 0.539.

exm-mc-scheffe-crime.title: Three slopes of a crime regression
exm-mc-scheffe-crime.title_html: Three slopes of a crime regression
exm-mc-scheffe-crime.html:
Return to the regression of the murder rate on poverty, single parenthood and urbanization for the 50 states of @exm-proj-fwl-crime, with ν=46 error degrees of freedom. The poverty coefficient is 0.2538 with standard error 0.0934, so t=2.718. Suppose the family of interest is every linear combination of the three slopes, q=3. The 95% intervals for the poverty coefficient are:

method multiplier interval
unadjusted t 2.013 [0.066, 0.442]
Bonferroni, three slopes 2.485 [0.022, 0.486]
Scheffé, all combinations 2.902 [−0.017, 0.525]

The poverty coefficient is significant on its own and among three planned comparisons, but not once every combination of the slopes is admitted. The F statistic for the hypothesis that all three slopes are zero is 27.49, and the largest |t| over all combinations is 9.081=3×27.49, in agreement with @eq-mc-scheffe-max.

exm-mc-scheffe-education.title: Education and the perceived position of a candidate
exm-mc-scheffe-education.title_html: Education and the perceived position of a candidate
exm-mc-scheffe-education.html:
The 1996 American National Election Study asked respondents to place Bill Clinton on a seven-point scale from extremely liberal (1) to extremely conservative (7). Group the n=944 respondents by education, coded from 1 (least) to 7 (most). The group sizes are 13, 52, 248, 187, 90, 227, 127, and the mean placements are 4.08, 3.58, 3.21, 2.95, 2.79, 2.66, 2.65. More educated respondents place Clinton further to the left. The pooled standard deviation is s=1.354 on ν=937 degrees of freedom, and the one-way F statistic is 7.88, with p-value 2.7×10−8. The between-groups sum of squares is 86.72.

Having seen the means, one might ask how the two least educated groups compare with the two most educated, the contrast ψ=12(μ1+μ2)−12(μ6+μ7). Its estimate is 1.176 with standard error 0.223, so t=5.27. Because the contrast was suggested by the data, the unadjusted t interval is not legitimate. The Scheffé interval @eq-mc-scheffe-contrasts, with multiplier 6F0.05(6,937)=3.557, is [0.383, 1.969], and it is legitimate however the contrast was found. The most significant contrast of all has t=6.88=6×7.88, and its sum of squares is the whole between-groups sum of squares.

exm-mc-tukey-education.title: All pairs of education levels
exm-mc-tukey-education.html: In @exm-mc-scheffe-education there are g=7 education levels, so 21 pairs, and ν=937. The Tukey–Kramer multiplier is q0.05(7,937)/2=4.179/2=2.955. It declares 9 of the 21 differences nonzero, against 14 for unadjusted t intervals (Section 13.6 compares all the methods). Figure 13.3.2 shows the intervals. The significant differences all separate a lower education level from a higher one, and the three most educated levels do not differ from one another. The smallest group, with only 13 respondents, has the highest mean, but its intervals are so wide that only its differences from levels 5, 6 and 7 are established.

exr-mc-bayes-shrink.title: C1
exr-mc-bayes-shrink.html: In the balanced one-way layout with known σ2, give the group means the prior μk∼iidN(μ0,τ2), with μ0 and τ2 known. Find the posterior distribution of μk−μl and compare the width and centre of its central 95% posterior interval with the unadjusted confidence interval. Explain in what sense the shrinkage addresses the multiplicity of comparisons, and in what sense it does not.

exr-mc-bh-adjusted.title: B1
exr-mc-bh-adjusted.html: Prove that BH at level q rejects H(i) iff the adjusted value @eq-mc-bh-adjusted satisfies p~(i)≤q.

exr-mc-bh-five.title: A1
exr-mc-bh-five.html: Apply the BH procedure at q=0.05 to the five p-values of @exr-mc-five-pvalues, and compute the adjusted p-values @eq-mc-bh-adjusted.

exr-mc-bh-fwer.title: B3
exr-mc-bh-fwer.html: With m0=2 true hypotheses with independent uniform p-values and m−2 false hypotheses whose p-values are 0, find the familywise error rate of BH at level q. Compare it with the false discovery rate given by @thm-mc-bh.

exr-mc-bh-holm.title: B2
exr-mc-bh-holm.html: Show that the BH procedure at level q rejects every hypothesis that Holm’s procedure at level q rejects. Hint: q/(m−i+1)≤iq/m for 1≤i≤m.

exr-mc-by.title: C1
exr-mc-by.html: Prove the Benjamini–Yekutieli bound: under arbitrary dependence, BH at level q/cm has false discovery rate at most m0q/m. Hint: write the false discovery rate as ∑i∈I0∑kPr(pi∈((j−1)q′m,jq′m], k^=k)/k summed over j≤k, with q′=q/cm, and exchange the order of summation.

exr-mc-choose.title: A1
exr-mc-choose.html: Choose a procedure for each situation, and say what family its guarantee refers to: (a) a trial with three doses and a placebo, where the protocol specifies the three comparisons with placebo; (b) eight fertilizers compared in a balanced field trial, with interest in every pair; (c) 5000 genes screened for association with a trait, to select candidates for a second study; (d) a contrast suggested by a plot of the group means.

exr-mc-control.title: B2
exr-mc-control.html: Treatments 1,…,g−1 are to be compared with a control, level 0, in a balanced layout. Show that the exact simultaneous multiplier for the g−1 differences μk−μ0 is the upper α point of maxk≥1|Zk−Z0|/V/ν, and that it is smaller than qα(g,ν).

exr-mc-duncan.title: B1
exr-mc-duncan.html: Show that under the global null the familywise error rate of Duncan’s procedure is 1−(1−α)g−1 in a balanced one-way layout.

exr-mc-fdr-not-fdp.title: A2
exr-mc-fdr-not-fdp.html: A report says: “Using BH at q=0.1 we made 40 discoveries, so at most 4 of them are false.” What is wrong with this statement? What would be a correct one?

exr-mc-fdr-small.title: A2
exr-mc-fdr-small.html: Give a configuration of true and false hypotheses, and a procedure, for which the familywise error rate is close to one while the false discovery rate is close to zero.

exr-mc-five-pvalues.title: A1
exr-mc-five-pvalues.html: Five hypotheses have p-values 0.001, 0.011, 0.012, 0.04, 0.2. At familywise level 0.05, which are rejected by Bonferroni’s procedure and which by Holm’s? Compute Holm’s adjusted p-values @eq-mc-holm-adjusted.

exr-mc-hochberg-holm.title: C1
exr-mc-hochberg-holm.html: Show that Hochberg’s step-up procedure rejects every hypothesis rejected by Holm’s step-down procedure with the same thresholds. Give an example with m=2 where Hochberg rejects both hypotheses and Holm rejects neither.

exr-mc-holm-adjusted.title: B1
exr-mc-holm-adjusted.html: Show that Holm’s procedure rejects H(i) iff the adjusted p-value @eq-mc-holm-adjusted satisfies p~(i)≤α, and that the adjusted p-values are nondecreasing in i.

exr-mc-holm-closed.title: B3
exr-mc-holm-closed.html: Show that Holm’s procedure is closed testing (@thm-mc-closed-testing) with the Bonferroni local tests ϕI: reject HI when mini∈Ipi≤α/|I|.

exr-mc-holm-pfer.title: B2
exr-mc-holm-pfer.html: All m≥2 hypotheses are true and the p-values are independent and uniform. Show that the per-family error rate of Bonferroni’s procedure is exactly α, while that of Holm’s procedure is larger than α. So Holm’s procedure controls the familywise rate but not the per-family rate.

exr-mc-independent-levels.title: A1
exr-mc-independent-levels.html: Ten and twenty independent tests of true hypotheses are made, each at level 0.01. Find the familywise error rate in each case. What common level for twenty independent tests gives a familywise rate of exactly 0.05?

exr-mc-lsd-limit.title: C1
exr-mc-lsd-limit.html: In a one-way layout with g≥3 groups of m observations and known σ, run the protected LSD with z tests: the gate is the level-α test that rejects when ∑km(y¯k−y¯)2/σ2 exceeds the upper α point of χ2(g−1), and a pair is declared different when |y¯k−y¯l|>zα/2σ2/m, where zα/2 is the upper α/2 point of N(0,1). Let μ1=⋯=μg−1=0 and μg=Δ. Show that as Δ→∞ the familywise error rate tends to Pr(Wg−1>2zα/2), where Wg−1 is the range of g−1 independent N(0,1) variables. Show that this limit is at least 1−(1−α)⌊(g−1)/2⌋ and that it tends to 1 as g→∞.

exr-mc-lsd-three.title: B1
exr-mc-lsd-three.html: Show that with g=3 groups the protected LSD controls the familywise error rate strongly. Hint: consider separately the configurations with three, one and no true equalities among the three pairwise hypotheses.

exr-mc-multivariate-t.title: C1
exr-mc-multivariate-t.html: Let 𝛌𝛌λ1,…,λk∈C(X⊤) be chosen in advance, with t statistics 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃Tj=(λj⊤β^−λj⊤β)/se(λj⊤β^). Show that (T1,…,Tk)=Z/(s/σ), where Z∼Nk(0,R) is independent of s, and R is the correlation matrix with entries 𝛌𝛌𝛌𝛌𝛌𝛌λi⊤Gλj/λi⊤Gλi⋅λj⊤Gλj. Deduce that the constant c with Pr(maxj|Tj|≤c)=1−α depends only on R and ν, and that it is at most the Bonferroni multiplier and at most Scheffé’s multiplier for the span of the 𝛌λj.

exr-mc-nk-limit.title: B2
exr-mc-nk-limit.html: In @exm-mc-newman-keuls with J pairs, let the separation between pairs tend to infinity. Show that the familywise error rate of Newman–Keuls converges to 1−Pr(|Tj|≤qα(2,ν)/2, j=1,…,J), where the Tj are t statistics with independent numerators and a common s. Using @prp-mc-sidak, show that the limit is at most 1−(1−α)J, and that it tends to this value as ν→∞.

exr-mc-q-two.title: A1
exr-mc-q-two.html: Prove @eq-mc-q-two, and deduce that Tukey’s intervals for g=2 are the ordinary t intervals.

exr-mc-range-test.title: B3
exr-mc-range-test.html: In the balanced one-way layout, the studentized range test rejects μ1=⋯=μg when Qobs=(maxky¯k−minky¯k)/(s/m)>qα(g,ν). Show that it has exact level α, and that it rejects iff some Tukey interval @eq-mc-tukey excludes 0. Show that the F test rejects iff ∑k(y¯k−y¯)2>(g−1)Fα(g−1,ν)s2/m, and describe, for g=3, configurations of the means that one test rejects and the other does not.

exr-mc-reduced-family.title: B1
exr-mc-reduced-family.html: Let C(X0)⊆C(X) with ranks r0<r, and V=C(M−M0). Show that a vector v∈C(X) lies in V iff 𝛍v⊤μ=0 for every 𝛍μ∈C(X0). Show that the maximum over v∈V of the squared t statistic for 𝛍v⊤μ=0 equals (r−r0)F, where F is the statistic of @thm-glh-f-test.

exr-mc-scheffe-one.title: A1
exr-mc-scheffe-one.html: Show that for q=1 Scheffé’s interval @eq-mc-scheffe-interval is the t interval of @thm-ci-estimable-interval, and explain why no multiplicity adjustment appears.

exr-mc-scheffe-shortest.title: C1
exr-mc-scheffe-shortest.html: Show that Scheffé’s multiplier cannot be reduced: if c<qFα(q,ν), the intervals 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃λ⊤β^±cse(λ⊤β^), 𝛌λ∈C(Λ), have simultaneous coverage less than 1−α. So among intervals of the form estimate ± constant × standard error, valid for the whole family, Scheffé’s are the shortest.

exr-mc-span-three.title: A2
exr-mc-span-three.html: In @exm-mc-scheffe-education, an analyst decides before seeing the data to examine the three contrasts 12(μ1+μ2)−12(μ6+μ7), μ1−μ7 and μ2−μ6. Show that they span a space of dimension 2, and state the Scheffé multiplier for this family.

exr-mc-tukey-two-way.title: B1
exr-mc-tukey-two-way.html: In a two-way additive model E(yijk)=μ+αi+βj with a rows, b columns and N observations in every cell, show that the column means y¯⋅j⋅ are independent, each with variance σ2/(aN), and independent of the residual mean square. Deduce Tukey intervals for all differences βj−βj′, and state their degrees of freedom.

exr-mc-unadjusted-fdr.title: B2
exr-mc-unadjusted-fdr.html: Let m0 true hypotheses have independent uniform p-values, and let m1 false hypotheses have p-values equal to 0. The unadjusted procedure rejects when pj≤α. Find its familywise error rate, show that its false discovery rate is at most m0α/m1, and conclude that the false discovery rate tends to 0 as m1→∞ with m0 fixed.

lem-mc-bh-leave-one-out.title: Replacing one p-value by zero
lem-mc-bh-leave-one-out.title_html: Replacing one p-value by zero
lem-mc-bh-leave-one-out.html: Fix i, and let k^(i) be the number of rejections of the BH procedure applied to the p-values with pi replaced by 0. Then k^(i) is a function of (pj)j≠i alone, and for each k=1,…,m, {Hi is rejected and k^=k}={pi≤kq/m and k^(i)=k}.

lem-mc-chebyshev.title: Chebyshev’s association inequality
lem-mc-chebyshev.html: Let U be a real random variable and f1,…,fk nonnegative, nondecreasing functions with Efj(U)k<∞. Then E[∏jfj(U)]≥∏jEfj(U).

lem-mc-projection-max.title: The largest standardized component
lem-mc-projection-max.html: Let V be a subspace of Rn with orthogonal projection PV, and let u∈Rn. Then maxv∈V, v≠0(v⊤u)2‖v‖2=‖PVu‖2, and if PVu≠0 the maximum is attained exactly at the nonzero multiples of PVu.

lem-mc-range-contrast.title: A contrast is bounded by the range
lem-mc-range-contrast.title_html: A contrast is bounded by the range
lem-mc-range-contrast.html: If ∑kck=0, then for all real x1,…,xg, |∑kckxk|≤12∑k|ck|(maxkxk−minkxk), with equality when c is a multiple of a pairwise difference ek−el and xk, xl are the largest and smallest of the x’s.

prp-mc-error-rate-order.title: How the error rates compare
prp-mc-error-rate-order.html: For every procedure and every value of the parameters, PCER≤FWER≤PFER,FDR≤FWER. If all the hypotheses are true (m0=m), then FDR=FWER. Consequently a procedure that controls the per-family error rate at α controls the familywise rate at α, and a procedure that controls the familywise rate controls the false discovery rate.

prp-mc-gatekeeper.title: A gate gives weak control
prp-mc-gatekeeper.html: Let ϕ0 be a level-α test of the global null H0. A procedure that rejects no Hj unless ϕ0 rejects H0 controls the familywise error rate weakly at level α.

prp-mc-intervals-to-tests.title: Tests from simultaneous intervals
prp-mc-intervals-to-tests.html:
Let [Lj,Uj], j∈J, be simultaneous confidence intervals at level 1−α, and for given constants dj reject Hj:ψj=dj exactly when dj∉[Lj,Uj]. Then:

  1. the probability of rejecting at least one true Hj is at most α, for every value of the parameters;

  2. if, whenever Hj is rejected, one also declares ψj>dj or ψj<dj according to the side of dj on which the interval lies, the probability of at least one false rejection or wrong declaration of sign is at most α.

prp-mc-sidak.title: Šidák intervals
prp-mc-sidak.html: Let Z1,…,Zk be independent N(0,1) variables and V∼χ2(ν) independent of them, and put Tj=Zj/V/ν. Then for every c>0, Pr(|Tj|≤c for all j)≥∏j=1kPr(|Tj|≤c). Consequently, if 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃λ1⊤β^,…,λk⊤β^ are uncorrelated, the intervals 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃λj⊤β^±cse(λj⊤β^) with c the upper 12(1−(1−α)1/k) point of t(ν) have simultaneous coverage at least 1−α.

prp-mc-tukey-shortest.title: Tukey’s intervals are the shortest for all pairs
prp-mc-tukey-shortest.title_html: Tukey’s intervals are the shortest for all pairs
prp-mc-tukey-shortest.html: In the balanced one-way model, suppose intervals y¯k−y¯l±cs2/m with a common multiplier c have simultaneous coverage at least 1−α for all pairs. Then c≥qα(g,ν)/2. In particular the Bonferroni, Šidák and Scheffé intervals for all pairs are at least as long as Tukey’s.

thm-mc-bh.title: Benjamini–Hochberg
thm-mc-bh.html: Suppose that for each true hypothesis Hi, i∈I0, the p-value pi is independent of the other m−1 p-values and satisfies Pr(pi≤u)≤u for 0≤u≤1. Then the BH procedure at level q has FDR≤m0mq≤q, with equality in the first inequality when every pi, i∈I0, is uniform on (0,1).

thm-mc-bonferroni.title: Bonferroni
thm-mc-bonferroni.html:
1. For any events A1,…,Am, Pr(⋃jAj)≤∑jPr(Aj).

  2. Let α1,…,αm>0 with ∑jαj=α. If [Lj,Uj] is a confidence interval for ψj with coverage at least 1−αj, for each j, then the m intervals have simultaneous coverage at least 1−α.

  3. Let pj be a p-value for Hj, valid in the sense that Pr(pj≤u)≤u for 0≤u≤1 whenever Hj is true. The procedure that rejects Hj when pj≤αj has PFER≤∑j∈I0αj≤α, and hence controls the familywise error rate strongly at level α.

No assumption is made about the dependence among the events, intervals or p-values.

thm-mc-closed-testing.title: Closed testing
thm-mc-closed-testing.html: The procedure that rejects Hj iff ϕI rejects HI for every I containing j controls the familywise error rate strongly at level α.

thm-mc-holm.title: Holm
thm-mc-holm.html:
Let each pj be valid for Hj, as in @thm-mc-bonferroni(c), with any dependence among them. Then:

  1. Holm’s procedure controls the familywise error rate strongly at level α;

  2. it rejects every hypothesis that Bonferroni’s procedure (all αj=α/m) rejects, and possibly more.

thm-mc-scheffe.title: Scheffé’s simultaneous intervals
thm-mc-scheffe.html:
Assume @eq-opt-normal-model with r<n, and let 0<α<1.

  1. Let V⊆C(X) be a subspace of dimension q≥1. Then 𝛍𝛍maxv∈V, v≠0(v⊤Y−v⊤μ)2qs2‖v‖2=‖PV(Y−μ)‖2/qs2∼F(q,ν), and consequently 𝛍Pr(|v⊤(Y−μ)|≤qFα(q,ν)s‖v‖  ∀v∈V)=1−α.

  2. Let Λ be p×q of rank q with C(Λ)⊆C(X⊤). With probability exactly 1−α, for every 𝛌λ∈C(Λ) simultaneously, 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃λ⊤β∈[λ⊤β^−qFα(q,ν)se(λ⊤β^),  λ⊤β^+qFα(q,ν)se(λ⊤β^)].{#eq-mc-scheffe-interval}

    Moreover, with 𝛉𝛃θ=Λ⊤β, 𝛉𝛃θ^=Λ⊤β^ and W=Λ⊤GΛ, 𝛌𝛌𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃𝛉𝛉𝛉𝛉maxλ∈C(Λ), λ≠0(λ⊤β^−λ⊤β)2se(λ⊤β^)2=(θ^−θ)⊤W−1(θ^−θ)s2,{#eq-mc-scheffe-max}

    attained at 𝛌𝛉𝛉λ=ΛW−1(θ^−θ).

thm-mc-tukey.title: Tukey’s simultaneous intervals
thm-mc-tukey.html:
In the balanced one-way model with normal errors, g≥2 and ν=g(m−1)≥1, let cT=qα(g,ν). Then:

  1. with probability exactly 1−α, μk−μl∈[y¯k−y¯l−cTsm,  y¯k−y¯l+cTsm]for all k≠l;{#eq-mc-tukey}

  2. on the same event, for every contrast ψ=∑kckμk, |∑kcky¯k−ψ|≤cTsm⋅12∑k|ck|, so these intervals for all contrasts also have simultaneous coverage exactly 1−α.
